Key implementation artifacts for this story:
1) Rule implementation exists and matches the story intent - File: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - Header explicitly ties to this story: - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md` - `@req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING`, `REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT`, `REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX`, `REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT`, `REQ-VALID-OUTPUT`, `REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION`, `REQ-AUTO-FIX`. - Optional warning behavior: - `analyzeComment` + `processComment` detect comments that contain both `@story` and `@req`. - If `@implements` is also present, reports `messageId: "cannotAutoFix"` with reason "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @implements annotations". - If multiple distinct story paths found (via `hasMultipleStories`), reports `messageId: "multiStoryDetected"`. - Otherwise reports `messageId: "preferImplements"`. - Auto-fix implementation: - `collectStoryAndReqMetadata(comment)` parses the block, collects: - `storyLineIndices`, `reqLineIndices`, `reqIds`, `storyPath`. - Only accepts simple forms: `@story ` and `@req `; more complex lines cause it to bail (storyPath set to null or no indices), preventing unsafe fixes. - `buildImplementsAutoFix(context, comment, storyPaths)`: - Requires `storyPaths.size === 1`, exactly one `@story` line, at least one `@req`, and non-null `storyPath`. - Creates a `Rule.ReportFixer` via `applyImplementsReplacement`. - `applyImplementsReplacement`: - Builds line: `@implements ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}`. - Derives prefix (indentation and `*`) from original @story line: `const prefixMatch = storyRawLine.match(/^(\s*\*?\s*)/)`. - Replaces the @story line with the @implements line, removes all @req lines, and joins the rest unchanged. - Uses `fixer.replaceTextRange` to replace the original block from `comment.range[0]` up to before the closing `*/`, preserving the `/*` prefix and adding `"*/"` at the end. - This satisfies: - Single story conversion (one @implements line with multiple REQ IDs). - Preservation of comment structure and order of non-removed lines. - Conservative behavior for complex patterns (no fix if ambiguous), which supports REQ-VALID-OUTPUT. - Rule meta: - `meta.type: "suggestion"` (recommendation rule). - `meta.fixable: "code"` (auto-fix enabled). - Messages exactly match the story’s examples: - `preferImplements`: "Consider using @implements instead of @story + @req for clearer traceability. Run ESLint with --fix to auto-convert." - `cannotAutoFix`: "Cannot auto-fix: {{reason}}. Manual migration to @implements required." - `multiStoryDetected`: "Multiple @story annotations detected in the same comment block. Manually convert to separate @implements lines."
2) Tests specifically for this story - File: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - Header: - `* Tests for: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md` - `* @story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md` - `* @req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING ...` - `* @req REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT ...` - `* @req REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY ...` - Uses `RuleTester` to validate behavior. - Valid cases (backward compatibility): - Comment with only `@story` → valid. - Comment with only `@req` → valid. - Comment with only `@implements` → valid. - These directly exercise REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION. - Invalid cases: - Single-story `@story + @req` triggers `preferImplements` and auto-fixes to one `@implements` line: - `output` is exactly `@implements REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`. - Single `@story` with multiple `@req` auto-fixes to `@implements REQ-ONE REQ-TWO REQ-THREE`. - Mixed `@story`/`@req` with `@implements` triggers `cannotAutoFix` with the expected reason string. - Multiple `@story` paths triggers `multiStoryDetected`. - Complex `@req` / complex `@story` cases still report `preferImplements` but have no `output`, so no fix is applied. - Together these cover REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT (via snapshot-like output), and REQ-VALID-OUTPUT.

4) Documentation for this rule/story - File: docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md - Header ties to this story and its REQs. - States this is an "Optional migration rule". - Shows configuration examples: - Demonstrates how to set the rule to "off", "warn", or "error" in user ESLint config. - Provides before/after auto-fix examples that match the story’s examples (single-story and multi-REQ).

traceability.notes:
Most of the functional aspects of Story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md have been implemented: there is a dedicated ESLint rule that detects legacy @story + @req usage, emits recommendation diagnostics, performs a conservative auto-fix that converts single-story @story/@req blocks (including multi-REQ cases) into a single @implements line while preserving formatting, and detects multi-story and mixed-annotation patterns that cannot be auto-fixed. There are clear, story-linked unit tests and accompanying documentation for the rule.
However, two critical issues prevent this story from being fully satisfied:
1) **Default severity/enablement does not match the spec.** The story explicitly requires that the recommendation rule be disabled by default (default off) to maintain backward compatibility. In contrast, the plugin’s exported `recommended` and `strict` configs configure `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as `"warn"` by default, and tests assert that behavior. This directly violates the REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY requirement and the acceptance criterion about default behavior.
2) **Tests for this rule are failing in the observed run.** Running Jest targeted at `tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts` via the standard `npm test` script exits with code 1, indicating that at least one assertion or test in this suite fails. The story’s Definition of Done requires that tests for auto-fix transformations, edge cases, and configuration be written **and passing**; this condition is not met in the current environment.
Because of these discrepancies—especially the incorrect default configuration and the failing test run—the implementation does not fully meet all acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done for this story. Therefore, the assessment status is FAILED.
